replacement: Read the incoming raw errno, call nix sysconf once, and restore the incoming value only when the call left zero errno; preserve nonzero native errors. Map None and Err to the existing -1 numeric sentinel, retaining the c_long-to-f64 cast. No dependency, public API, version or times arithmetic change. Remove one lexical block; compiled CPU-native spans decrease Linux four to two and macOS six to four; Windows unchanged.
local_baseline: Two clock_tick_contracts tests passed (/tmp/martensite-clock-ticks-baseline.log); the full gate passed (/tmp/martensite-clock-ticks-baseline-pr.log).
contract: clock_ticks returns libc sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK) cast to f64, including -1 on failure. It supplies the divisor for process CPU time; the times call and arithmetic remain outside this increment.
fixtures: Compare against the native getconf CLK_TCK utility, then separately probe successful-query errno preservation using zero, EIO and an arbitrary raw sentinel. Restore the caller errno before assertions. These are native system-boundary checks, not mocked command-I/O tests.
candidate: Existing nix 0.31.3 unistd::sysconf exposes CLK_TCK and returns Result<Option<c_long>>. Inspected source clears errno before calling libc exactly once; unlike the direct call, that can erase a caller errno. Safe Errno::last_raw and set_raw can restore the incoming value when the call leaves zero errno. Mapping None and Err to -1 preserves the numeric sentinel; retain any nonzero errno produced by the native call.
limits: Native baseline fixtures establish supported-platform successful-query behavior, not every injected libc implementation. Incoming-errno-dependent interposed implementations are not covered. Processor counts and system-only exceptions remain outside this increment.
deletion: Deleted the direct sysconf unsafe block; no parallel implementation remains. No public API or version change.
